candidates.name: Cathédrale St-Pierre and Calvin's auditorium
candidates.price: Adults Fr. 16 (Seniors, Disabled, Students aged 16-25, and groups of more than 15 qualify for a Fr. 10 pass, children aged 7-16 qualify for an Fr. 8 pass. Entry to the church itself is free, of course, but donations are welcome.)
candidates.content: The new Espace Saint Pierre pass includes entrance to all three sites of Cour Saint-Pierre, a worthy space of unique spiritual and cultural importance. The Cathedral and its towers, originally Catholic, both embody the high point

candidates.name: International Museum of the Reformation
candidates.price: Fr. 10 for Adults; Seniors, Disabled, Students from 16-25 years old qualify for a Fr. 7 admission fee; Children age 7-16 years old and groups of 15 or more qualify for a Fr. 5 admission fee; Children under 7 are free. For another Fr. 3, you can explore the archaeological site beneath the cathedral and climb the tower inside the cathedral, which has some amazing views of the city
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and on 1 January. Open Easter, Pentecost, and Jeune Federal Mondays. Access for disabled visitors.
candidates.content: Installed on the ground floor of the magnificent Maison Mallet (next to Saint-Pierre Cathedral), this new Museum presents the main spiritual and cultural elements of the Reformation. Unique objects, manuscripts, rare books, engrav

candidates.name: Museum of the International Committee of the Red Cross
candidates.price: Adult Fr. 15; child, ICRC members, the elderly, and others Fr. 7
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and on 1 January. Access for disabled visitors.
candidates.content: The Museum of the ICRC is in the basement of the headquarters and shows photos and objects related to the organisation's service to humanity during countless wars and natural disasters, and presents stories of victims. However muc

candidates.name: Musée Ariana
candidates.content: Occupying a big chunk of what would otherwise be the UN campus, the Ariana Museum offers a huge collection (16,000 pieces) of ceramics from around Europe and the Far East.

candidates.name: Musée d'Art et d'Histoire
candidates.content: Extensive art and archaeological-historical collections. Painting gallery extends back to the early Renaissance, but is most extensive in Swiss-French and Impressionist works.

candidates.name: CERN Science Gateway
candidates.content: The CERN particle physics research centre has a purpose built museum presenting the history of CERN, our universe and quantum science at a level accessible to all. Almost all exhibits are interactive and are presented in five lang

candidates.name: Musée d'Art Moderne et Contemporain
candidates.content: Late modern, post-modern, and contemporary works by internationally known artists, as well as a special collection of Swiss conceptual work.

candidates.name: Musée d'Histoire Naturelle
candidates.content: Geneva has a nice museum which is worth a visit, especially if you have youth and children.

candidates.name: Jet d'Eau
candidates.hours: daily 10:00-23:00 (shut off in November for maintenance and during strong winds.)
candidates.content: One of the crowning symbols of Geneva is the monumental Jet d'Eau, a fountain of water pumped 140m into the air. The spectacular plume was once an occasional pressure release for hydro-power generation on the Rhône River, but peop

candidates.name: Palais des Nations
candidates.price: Fr. 12 each for adults (groups of 20 adults or more qualify for a 20% discount; private tour of 1-14 adults Fr. 127.50; Fr. 10 each for students, senior citizens, and disabled persons; Fr. 4 for schoolchildren; free for children under six years old)
candidates.hours: Open daily Apr-Oct: 10:00-12:00 and 14:00-16:00; Jul-Aug 10:00-17:00; the rest of the year Mon-Fri 10:00-12:00 and 14:00-16:00 (except over the Christmas period)
candidates.content: Built to house the League of Nations, the Palais is worth visiting just to take in the magnificent Assembly Hall, in addition to the large collection of public art, the library, and the landscaped grounds. Visits are by guided tou

candidates.name: Monument Brunswick
candidates.content: An impressive monument, constructed in 1873 as a Mausoleum for the Duke of Brunswick, as a replica of the tomb of the Scaligeri family in Verona (14th century). Also worth visiting for the 5-star hotels and the cars in front of th

candidates.name: Patek Philippe Museum
candidates.price: Adults Fr. 10, Seniors/people with disabilities/unemployed/students Fr. 7, under 18 years old free
candidates.content: Four floors of stunningly beautiful watches and clocks from the last centuries, both Patek Philippe and other brands. There is also a section presenting watchmaking in practice. Bags (even shopping bags) must be kept in free locke

candidates.name: Maison Tavel
candidates.content: Three floors presenting the history of Geneva from the Middle Ages until the 19th century. There's an entrance fee to the temporary exhibitions in the basement.

candidates.name: Old Town
candidates.content: Aside of the cathedral the Old town in general is worth walking around in for an hour or two. Among the highlights are the city hall with the cannons in the little square opposite to it, Rousseau's birth house and various antique

candidates.name: L'Ile
candidates.content: Worth visiting for the old Tour de L'Ile, the remains of a fortified castle erected in the 13th century.

candidates.name: Eaux-Vives
candidates.content: While many of Geneva's buildings are similar in style to what you would find in French cities, the Mairie of Eaux-Vives is a great example of the typical Swiss architecture you would find in cities like Zürich. If you're intereste

candidates.name: Fondation Baur, Musée des Arts d’Extrême-Orient
candidates.content: The largest collections of Far Eastern art open to the public in Switzerland. Temporary exhibitions are regularly organized several times a year.

candidates.name: Musée d'histoire des sciences
candidates.content: Museum dedicated to scientists who've lived and worked in Geneva. You can see old equipment from telescopes to galvanometers and glass eyes.

candidates.name: Quartier des Grottes
candidates.content: An area with interesting shops and most importantly, a series of residential buildings called "les Schtroumpfs" (1982-1984), where the architects tried to avoid all straight lines, leading to an unconventional Gaudi-like appearanc

candidates.name: Île Rousseau
candidates.content: Small island where the lake ends and river Rhône begins named after the famous philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau - of course there's a statue of him there too.

candidates.name: Jardin botanique
candidates.content: At the botanical garden you can see flowers, plants and trees both from the Alps and from other parts of the world. The palm house also hosts tropical vegetation. In the northern part of the park there is a zoo spread over a quite

candidates.name: Place Neuve
candidates.content: See the impressive Grand Theatre (1879, renovated after a fire in 1951), the Conservatoire de musique, and the Musée Rath. Also visit the Parc des Bastions, which includes a large wall ("Mur des Réformateurs") showing some of the

candidates.name: Carouge
candidates.content: A district of Geneva that once belonged to the Kingdom of Sardinia and hence retains a distinct Italian flavour.

candidates.name: Salève cable car
candidates.content: Just over the French border, this high alpine ridge has a stunning view of Mt. Blanc and the Lake Geneva area and miles of walking trails. A cute little corner shop in Pas de l'Échelle Village (France) sells about 100 varieties of

candidates.name: Fête de la Musique
candidates.content: For three days in June, the whole City of Geneva is a stage. Actually, there are on the order of 40 of them. The musical offerings include children's choirs, punk rock, chamber orchestras, jam bands, avant-guard jazz, klezmer, and

candidates.name: Genève Plage
candidates.content: There are many smaller places where to swim in either the rivers or the lake, but the largest one is Genève Plage (literally "Geneva Beach") at the eastern bank of the lake. It's a nice place to swim, enjoy the sun, play, barbecue

candidates.name: Fêtes de la Batie
candidates.content: A 16-day arts festival (usually starts the last weekend of July and through most of August) with installations and live shows in over 20 venues across the city. Very similar in feel to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival. 2025 is operat

candidates.name: Bois de la Bâtie
candidates.content: Just over the river Arve from Jonction. Most of this woodsy bluff has been left in a more-or-less natural state, though there are walking trails around the edges. The trails connect eventually with a sidewalk which crosses a railr

candidates.name: Jardin Anglais
candidates.content: A small park where people like to spend their lunch break. Located at the bank of Lake Geneva, just as you've crossed over the Mont Blanc bridge to the southern half of the city. In the summer there are many small concerts and fun

candidates.name: Association Genevoise des Amis du Salève
candidates.content: Organizes free hikes around Geneva every Sunday. Start at 10:00 (sharp) at terminus (End station) of bus number 8 at Veyrier-Douane.

candidates.name: L'Escalade
candidates.content: Running and walking competitions open to everybody.

candidates.name: Parc des Bastions
candidates.content: This lovely tree lined park, which is home to the liberal arts campus of the University of Geneva features giant chessboards and even larger statues of Geneva's Calvinist founding fathers, and it's directly between the old town an

candidates.name: Parc des Eaux Vives
candidates.content: This park offers promenades and views over the lake of the UN campus and the Palais des Nations. Geneva beach is at the end furthest from the city, on the lakefront.

candidates.name: Parc de la Grange
candidates.content: Just along the south side of the Lake Geneva promenade, Parc de la Grange is a large park which contains a rose garden, a historic mansion and a tree-lined path leading to the nearby Parc des Eaux Vives.

candidates.name: La Perle du Lac
candidates.content: Translates to the "Pearl of the Lake" and is the largest park on the western bank of Lake Geneva. It hosts the splendid eponymous restaurant and a free science museum, but it also a great place for a picnic.

candidates.name: Caves Ouvertes
candidates.content: Free annual event. Sample wine at Geneva's wineries while exploring the canton's rural side.

candidates.name: Bol d'Or
candidates.content: Yacht Race (biggest in Europe).

candidates.name: Les Brasseurs
candidates.hours: Tue to Sat until 02:00, Sun and Mon until 00:00
candidates.content: One of the few brew pubs in Geneva, Les Brass serves three flavours of home brew in the usual half pints, pints, and litre glasses or you can go for one of the giant plastic tubes filled with three to five litres. A small menu of

candidates.name: Le Ferblanterie
candidates.price: Fr. 3/6 draft/bottle beers. A glass of wine is about the same
candidates.content: The Ferblanterie, or Tinsmith would be one of the coolest bars in just about any town, and it happens to be on a street loaded with cool bars. This is very much a student haunt, and a grungy one in all the right ways. Some of the

candidates.name: L'Etabli
candidates.price: Fr. 3/6 draft/bottle beers. A glass of wine is about the same.
candidates.content: L'Etabli is a great place to go when the Ferblanterie is packed, or perhaps it's the other way around. This super-friendly little café/bar/wine bar is a great place to meet grad students to help with your French, or to help with t

candidates.name: Pickwicks
candidates.content: One of the half-dozen or so British pubs, Pickwicks claims to be the largest pub in Switzerland. Usually full of football watching expats eating fish and chips while sipping Guinness. Friday and Saturday night usually features liv

candidates.name: Alhambar
candidates.content: A swanky cocktail bar above the Alhambra Theater. Pretty people in a pretty room, usually with a DJ. A small tapas menu early in the evening and a nice brunch on weekends until 14:00.

candidates.name: La Clémence
candidates.content: This cozy little bar on the central square of Geneva's old town more than quintuples in size from April until October when it is able to use a huge swath of the place as its terrace. During warm weather it's packed, but is such a

candidates.name: Saveurs & Couleurs Café
candidates.content: The Grottes neighbourhood of Geneva has long been a centre for creative types, many of whom can be found of an evening enjoying a glass of wine at this comfy little bistro.

candidates.name: Les Enfants Terribles
candidates.content: A café bar bicycle-workshop hair salon and wine shop, with a nice lunch tapas buffet and Thursday night jazz in a beautiful post-industrial space with atrium roofs and an olive tree. What is there not to like?

candidates.name: Grand Duke Pub
candidates.content: One of the oldest English pubs in Geneva. Live sports, wide selection of draught and bottled beers, ciders. More than 5 big television screens are there to watch different sports as well as a good area to play darts. You can enjoy

candidates.name: Mulligans Irish Pub
candidates.content: You will be guaranteed a great time at this centrally located pub. Good music most nights. Bands often play on Thursday and Friday evenings. A good lively crowd who know how to party. Guinness, Bulmers, Staropramen, Boddingtons, s

candidates.name: Remor
candidates.content: Really the best Parisien-style grande café in Geneva. Artwork by University Students and sometimes the Proprietor hang on the wall. They also offer two salads of the day, and a range of ice-cream treats. They screen the best of Sw

candidates.name: Bypass
candidates.content: One of the most modern clubs in Geneva, the Bypass is, for lack of a better word, bling-bling. The dance floor swarms with young professionals and, on occasion, corporate parties and the rooms pound with clean house music, hip-hop

candidates.name: Shakers
candidates.content: This club is known for the wild nights within, thanks to its very strong cocktails served in shaker glasses. The dance floor is imposing, but once on it, well known for romantic encounters. Very popular with English speakers.

candidates.name: Weetamix
candidates.content: Although it's not the easiest place to get to, Weetamix is able to attract good, mostly local crowds by consistently booking some of the best cutting-edge talent in electronic music from France, Britain, and the U.S..

candidates.name: Espresso Club
candidates.content: A tiny bar and three tables means this little local spot is usually packed with a very international crowd of people who know where to get the best pizza, salads, and pasta dishes in town, with many vegetarian selections. Espresso

candidates.name: La feuille de banane
candidates.content: One of the best ratios of food quality to price in Geneva for Asiatic food. For around Fr. 10, you can have a tasty meal with chicken, beef or fish, and various choices of sauces. The service is ultra fast since everything is

candidates.name: Edward's The fine art of sandwiches
candidates.content: Packed with locals at lunchtime and for a reason - delicious warm sandwiches and cakes. On the downside it is a bit hectic and it might be difficult to find a seat.

candidates.name: Le Montparnasse
candidates.price: mains Fr. 20-40, but has lunch specials and the three-course "Menu of the day" for Fr. 30
candidates.content: French and Swiss cuisine and a healthy "antidote" to the extremely touristy restaurants serving Swiss food. Most of the visitors are older locals who drop in for a few glasses of wine and a chat with the owner. Try the menu of the

candidates.name: Buvette des Bains (Bains des Paquis)
candidates.content: Wonderful place in the middle of the lake. Beach in Summer, fondue restaurant in Winter. Good "plat du jour" all day for Fr. 12

candidates.name: Café Art's
candidates.content: Café Art's (sic) has a limited menu of salads and pasta dishes, but all around or under Fr. 15 and service is non-stop all day.

candidates.name: Sing Fa la maison du Ravioli (Sing Fa dumpling house)
candidates.hours: morning-midnight (closed on Mon lunch), opened 7 days a week
candidates.content: Serves fairly authentic Chinese dumplings and noodles.

candidates.name: Asia Garden
candidates.content: Large selection of Chinese and Japanese dishes. Quality Chinese food (it's always full of Chinese customers) but no fancy atmosphere.

candidates.name: Piment Vert
candidates.content: Indian and Sri Lankan fast food in a charmingly appointed space. There's also a terrace during warm weather.

candidates.name: Chez Ma Cousine
candidates.content: A chain with a simple menu: chicken, chicken, or chicken. The roasted chicken is what they're famous for, and two chicken salads make the rest of the regular menu, each under Fr. 14.90.

candidates.name: Manora
candidates.content: Cafeteria like serving area with everything and anything including (but not inclusive): chicken, pasta, pizza, desserts, entree of the day, salads, and coffee. Great view of the Geneva skyline from the balcony eating area.

candidates.name: Boulangerie Tea-Room Deux-Ponts
candidates.content: Portuguese "tea room" serving sandwiches, bifanas (hot sandwiches) and pastries that are fresh, delicious, large and don't cost very much. The catch: they don't have very much on display so you can't just point at stuff but need t

candidates.name: Flea market at Plainpalais
candidates.content: If you like flea markets and shuffling through old stuff like vinyl records, books, chinaware etc., especially stuff with a Swiss and French background and happen to be in Geneva on a Saturday (or some Wednesdays), Plainpalais squ
